messages.subject: Quick note about Nell — nothing to worry about
messages.body:
Hello,

I wanted to write before the newsletter goes out, because a form letter is a strange way to hear good news.

Nell read out loud to the class on Wednesday. She chose the piece herself and she stood up to do it without being asked, which is a first this year. It was three paragraphs about the old rail bridge and where the track used to go, and she had clearly gone and looked it up somewhere rather than making it up.

She stumbled twice and carried on both times. That is the part I wanted you to know about.

Her spelling is still where it was in the summer and we will keep working on it. No action needed from you. I just thought you would like Friday to start well.

Best wishes,
Funmi Adeyemi
Year 4, Halsey Primary

messages.subject: you won't remember me but
messages.body:
I found an old backup this weekend while I was looking for something else, and in it was a folder of forum posts from 2004 to about 2007. Yours were in there. Mine were in there, which was worse.

I don't know if this address still reaches you. It was on the sign-up list for the Gridfall boards meet in 2006, the one where four of us turned up at the Blue Kestrel and it had already closed and we stood in the car park for an hour anyway.

I kept the boards going for a while. They are still up, technically. [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]boards.gridfall.net[/url] loads and the posts are all there, but nothing on the front page since 2011 was written by a person. Someone runs a bot that bumps old threads with a summary of themselves. It gets the tone about eighty percent right, which I find harder to look at than if it were bad.

Anyway. I am in Marchfield now, back in the county after twenty years, and I have a garage full of boxes and no one to show them to.

The model of the branch line on the classifieds this week is Ray Vosper's. I met him once. If you have not seen it, look before Saturday: [url=synth://classifieds.verity.net/]classifieds.verity.net[/url]

No need to reply. I mostly wanted to type your name into a To field again and see what happened.

— Tom

messages.subject: Saturday
messages.body:
Thank you for saying you would come on Saturday and help with the tables.

I put the three listings up on the classifieds and by the evening I had forty-one messages. Thirty-eight were from the same four accounts offering to buy everything at once, sight unseen, collection Thursday. One of them addressed me as Ray.

The other three were people. One is a man from the rail forum who says he knew the layout. He asked if he could come an hour early and just look at it before anybody else arrives. I said yes.

Come at half eight if you can. Bring a flask, the kettle is packed.

Ellen

messages.subject: Ray
messages.body:
I am writing to the people whose addresses were in his book, so forgive me if this is abrupt.

Ray died on Tuesday morning at home. It was quick and I was with him.

The service is on the 29th at eleven, at St. Bride's in Ashkettle. No flowers. If you knew him from the railway, he would have liked it if you wore something with a number on it, which was a joke he made for thirty years and I am going to keep making it for him.

Ellen
